answer: Each identity claims a zenith settling column, registers a ferrous ore sample, locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch files violet dye-front height at 1, 5, 10 minutes; an auditor checks heights on the public ferrous-settling table and burns the bond for a 3% deviation, a reused serial, or a filing past zenith noon. First filing 39 credits, k-th 39+7(k-1); so 1000 fakes pay 3,535,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-column ring fails: a borrowed column bears its lender's etched serial, so one front cannot match two ore grades. An honest keeper pays 39 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
